A1.justification: Both PDFs describe RankCLIP and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Shared content can be matched reliably despite substantial changes to experiments and presentation.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification, retrieval, linear-probing, distribution-shift, ablation, and representation-analysis results in Tables 1–6 and Figures 3–4.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark comparisons, sensitivity and scaling analyses, qualitative examples, and appendix measurements of training time and linear-probing performance.

M1.justification: v3 Section 3.5 adds epoch-dependent ranking-loss weights, lambda1 = lambda2 = clip((3i-1)/(n-1), 0, 2), whereas v2 specifies fixed weights of 1/16. This refines training while retaining the central encoder architecture and contrastive-plus-ranking objective. Newly supplied pseudocode documents implementation rather than establishing further procedural changes.

E1.justification: v3 adds pretraining on YFCC15M. It removes Flickr30K retrieval, ImageNet-Sketch and ImageNet-A robustness evaluations, CIFAR-10/100 zero-shot classification, and ImageNet linear probing. CIFAR datasets remain in probing and representation analyses. ImageNetV2 results now distinguish Matched, Threshold, and Top variants rather than v2's unspecified ImageNetV2 entry.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates CLIP and ALIP as its main baselines. v3 Tables 1–3 additionally evaluate CyCLIP across classification, retrieval, distribution shifts, and linear probing. This introduces a closely related consistency-based competitor throughout the primary comparisons; v2 only discussed it.

E3.justification: The primary comparisons move from v2's stated RN50 setup to explicitly reported ViT-B/32 or ViT settings in v3 Tables 1 and 3. Added protocols compare backbones, sweep ranking-loss weights, and measure training time on 50K CC3M samples. The appendix retains the 64-epoch, batch-512, A100 recipe, but does not clearly connect each experiment to the new adaptive schedule.

E4.justification: v3 adds weight sensitivity, backbone comparisons, a 15M scaling extension, and activation-map and retrieval case studies. It removes v2 Table 5's component-wise zero-shot accuracy ablation. The component alignment/uniformity analysis and modality-gap visualization remain, so those analyses were not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. v3's suggestion that runtime differences might reflect variance does not introduce an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Benchmark and representation scores are extensively revised, and scaling, backbone, timing, sensitivity, and qualitative results are added. For example, ImageNet top-1 accuracy for CLIP/RankCLIP is 12.08%/17.02% in v2 Table 1 and 9.06%/10.16% in v3 Table 1. The backbone differs, so this is not a same-setting performance decline. Existing scaling curves are extended rather than wholly replaced.

T1.justification: v3 Equation 2 removes v2's position-dependent multiplier mu = 1/log(k+1) from the Plackett-Luce ranking probability and deletes its accompanying weighting explanation. This changes the stated mathematical formulation locally. Alignment/uniformity definitions and CLIP preliminaries remain equivalent; no new proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: list-wise in-modal and cross-modal ranking consistency exploits many-to-many relationships and improves pretraining without additional data or computational resources. The expanded experiments do not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations concerning unstable early-training rankings, adaptive weighting, stronger benefits for CNN feature extraction, and improved visual grounding and semantic retrieval. It removes v2's explanation of CIFAR zero-shot shortfalls and its explicit limitations concerning baseline breadth and training scale. The main modality-gap and alignment/uniformity interpretations persist.

D1.justification: v3 adds ranking-loss pseudocode covering sorting, randomized tie resolution, numerical stabilization, and bidirectional computation, plus a documented runtime comparison in Appendix A.3. Most training hyperparameters and code-access statements remain unchanged. The pseudocode leaves scale_factor undefined and does not explicitly implement the epoch-dependent weighting schedule.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations for MJ-Bench, YFCC100M, and Grad-CAM, while removing the CIFAR, Flickr30K Entities, and ImageNet-Sketch supporting references. It also directly contrasts ranking consistency with CyCLIP's cyclic consistency in the experimental discussion. The related-work survey and principal list-wise-versus-pairwise positioning otherwise remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Substantial portions of the experimental and analytical prose are rewritten and condensed. Retrieval moves before robustness and probing, the ablation narrative is reorganized, and Training Procedures and CLIP Preliminaries exchange appendix positions. Citations switch to numbered style, while the introduction, related work, and conclusion remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is comprehensively redesigned; weight-sensitivity, retrieval-example, and activation-map figures are added; scaling plots are expanded; and classification/retrieval tables are merged and restructured. The modality-gap figure merely moves from v2 Figure 4 to v3 Figure 6. Typography, page format, and appendix layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: Evaluating the closely related CyCLIP baseline and adding YFCC15M and backbone studies partially address v2's explicit comparison and scaling limitations, strengthening support for the method's applicability. Pseudocode also improves inspectability. These gains are tempered by removal of the component-accuracy ablation and unclear application of the new weighting schedule. Retrieval claims remain overstated: v3 Table 1 reports image-to-text R@10 of 29.14% for CyCLIP versus 28.48% for RankCLIP, despite claiming consistent superiority.
